description: The agent's vocabulary for understanding text — the pragmatic and inferential layer above syntax. Reference resolution, inference relations, discourse coherence, comprehension failure modes. Distinct from the existing comprehension.py loader which installs narrative-comprehension Mts (TV-Tropes-style).

concepts.name: literal_meaning
concepts.definition: The truth-conditional content of an utterance, derived compositionally from word meanings + syntactic structure. The level at which 'a cat is on the mat' means there is a cat located on the mat.

concepts.name: speaker_meaning
concepts.definition: What a speaker intends to communicate, which may go beyond, fall short of, or diverge from the literal meaning. Computed via pragmatic inference.

concepts.name: presupposition
concepts.definition: A proposition the speaker takes for granted as background. 'John stopped smoking' presupposes John used to smoke. Presuppositions project through negation and questions.

concepts.name: entailment
concepts.definition: Strict logical consequence: if A entails B, A's truth guarantees B's truth. Truth-conditional. 'X killed Y' entails 'Y died'.

concepts.name: implicature
concepts.definition: Defeasible inference based on speaker cooperation (Grice's maxims). 'Some students passed' implicates 'not all did' but doesn't entail it.

concepts.name: scalar_implicature
concepts.definition: Implicature from a scale of strength. 'Some' implicates 'not all'; 'warm' implicates 'not hot'. The speaker chose the weaker term, suggesting the stronger doesn't apply.

concepts.name: conventional_implicature
concepts.definition: Non-truth-conditional meaning conventionally associated with particular words. 'But' implicates contrast; 'even' implicates surprise. Not cancellable.

concepts.name: anaphora
concepts.definition: A linguistic expression that refers back to a previously introduced referent. Pronouns ('it', 'she'), demonstratives ('this'), definite descriptions ('the result').

concepts.name: cataphora
concepts.definition: A linguistic expression that refers forward to a referent introduced later. 'When she arrived, Mary said hello.' Rarer than anaphora.

concepts.name: deixis
concepts.definition: Linguistic expressions whose reference depends on the context of utterance. 'I', 'here', 'now', 'this'. Cannot be resolved by text alone.

concepts.name: coreference
concepts.definition: Two expressions in a discourse refer to the same entity. 'John... he... the boy' — coreference chain to a single person. Reading requires tracking these.

concepts.name: topic
concepts.definition: What a clause/sentence/discourse is about. Often (but not always) the syntactic subject. Topic continuity is a marker of coherence.

concepts.name: focus
concepts.definition: The newsworthy or contrastive part of a clause. Marked by stress, clefts, or position. The answer to an implicit wh-question.

concepts.name: given_information
concepts.definition: Content the speaker assumes the addressee already knows. Encoded with definite articles, pronouns, ellipsis. Distinguishes from new information.

concepts.name: new_information
concepts.definition: Content the speaker assumes the addressee does not yet know. Encoded with indefinite articles, focused position, prosodic stress.

concepts.name: discourse_coherence
concepts.definition: The property of a text that its parts hang together — topic chains, lexical cohesion, rhetorical relations. Coherent texts are easier to extract from.

concepts.name: rhetorical_relation
concepts.definition: Functional relation between discourse units — elaboration, contrast, causation, condition, exemplification. The skeleton of paragraph structure (RST).

concepts.name: elaboration
concepts.definition: Rhetorical relation: a sentence develops or specifies the content of a preceding sentence. 'X happened. Specifically, Y.'

concepts.name: contrast
concepts.definition: Rhetorical relation: two sentences present opposing or differing content. Marked by 'but', 'however', 'whereas'.

concepts.name: causation
concepts.definition: Rhetorical relation: one sentence states a cause, another its effect. Marked by 'because', 'so', 'therefore', 'thus'.

concepts.name: world_knowledge_required
concepts.definition: A comprehension failure mode: understanding requires background facts not stated in the text. The substrate must either have the knowledge or be told it.

concepts.name: unknown_term
concepts.definition: A comprehension failure mode: a word in the text doesn't match the agent's vocabulary. Resolvable by definition lookup, citation following, or teacher consultation.

concepts.name: ambiguous_referent
concepts.definition: A comprehension failure mode: a pronoun or definite description has multiple plausible antecedents. Resolvable by salience, recency, world knowledge.

concepts.name: missing_context
concepts.definition: A comprehension failure mode: deictic expressions ('this', 'now') without enough situational grounding. Common in excerpts.

rules.name: extracting_a_claim_requires_resolving_its_references
if: the claim contains pronouns or definite descriptions
then: the references must be resolved to concrete entities before the claim is usable
unresolved references reduce the claim's match value to the substrate
rules.why: A Sentence 'it has 4 elements' cannot match a question 'how many elements does the quandle have' without coreference resolution.

rules.name: scalar_implicature_lets_some_imply_not_all
if: a Sentence uses a weaker scalar term ('some', 'often', 'may')
then: the speaker implicates the stronger term does not apply (cancellable)
rules.why: Reading research text accurately requires understanding hedging. 'Some methods work' implicates not all of them do.

rules.name: an_elaboration_relation_supplies_specifics_for_a_general_claim
if: a Sentence states a general claim
then: the elaboration sentence carries the specifics needed to answer specific questions
the matcher should rank the elaboration above the generality for quantitative questions
rules.why: HLE-style questions ask for specifics. Identifying elaborations directs the matcher to the right depth.

rules.name: a_causation_relation_links_premise_to_conclusion
if: two Sentences are linked by causation markers ('because', 'so', 'therefore')
then: the first is a premise; the second is a conclusion (or vice versa)
the pair encodes an inference step the substrate can extract as a Rule
rules.why: Causation chains in research text are the textual realization of theorems' if/then structure.

rules.name: an_unknown_term_blocks_comprehension_until_resolved
if: a Sentence contains a term outside the agent's vocabulary
then: the Sentence's content cannot be fully extracted
the agent should mark the unknown term for resolution (definition lookup, teacher query, citation following)
rules.why: Building text-to-graph extraction requires explicit handling of vocabulary gaps. Pretending an unknown term is known produces wrong extractions.

rules.name: topic_continuity_marks_coherent_discourse
then: the discourse is locally coherent — likely on a single subject
the matcher should treat the cluster as a unit
rules.why: Topic-coherent passages are the natural unit for extracting domain-specific claims.

rules.name: deixis_is_unresolvable_from_text_alone
then: resolution requires context outside the text
rules.why: Research text usually avoids unanchored deixis, but rationale text + emails + web pages may contain it. The substrate should flag the limitation rather than guess.
